speakers: Richard Brennan (guest, systematic trend-following manager and researcher)
summary:
Brennan argues markets are complex adaptive systems whose price behaviour is driven by endogenous feedback; passive investing (price-insensitive, about 60% of US equity funds) dilutes balancing agents and thins the price-sensitive float, making trends, overshoots and cascades more likely.
He presents an agent-based model (about 25% chartists produces a phase transition) matching the statistical fingerprint of 68 futures markets over 40 years, concluding trend following harvests a structural, hardening feature. Also covers May 2026 CTA numbers, a SocGen sentiment survey and ATR sizing.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: the most commonly cited figure puts passive at around about 60% of US equity fund assets
claims.claim: Passive vehicles hold about 60% of US equity fund assets, and price-insensitive ownership including benchmark-hugging institutions is meaningfully higher.
claims.indicator: passive share of US equity fund assets

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: capital that allocates by index weight rather than price judgment is now a structural presence in markets well beyond US equities
claims.claim: The rise of passive via ETFs extends to fixed income, commodities, currency and multi-asset products, so the structural argument applies across asset classes.
claims.testable: partly - ownership data by asset class

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: each adapting to what others are doing, and each changing the environment that everyone else must respond to
claims.claim: Markets are complex adaptive systems whose prices, trends and cascades emerge from interactions of many participants with partial information, not from any one decision.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: Different ecologies produce different market behavior.
claims.claim: The mix of participants (the agent ecology: value, passive, momentum, vol-targeting, dealers) determines how a market behaves, so who is at the table matters.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: what kind of agents populate that system, and what are the properties of the interactions between them
claims.claim: The key question about a market is which agents populate it and how they interact, not fair value, macro backdrop or central bank action; fundamentals are loosely coupled autonomous systems.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: A momentum algorithm buys what is rising, not what is cheap. A volatility targeting fund reduces exposure when volatility rises, not when prices fall.
claims.claim: Momentum algos, vol-targeting funds and stop losses are price-sensitive in the amplifying direction, while value investors, counter-trend traders, market makers and rebalancing pensions absorb moves.
claims.testable: partly - flow models for vol targeting and CTAs

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: passive is not price sensitive. And because it's not price sensitive, it does not participate in price discovery.
claims.claim: Passive allocates by index rule regardless of price, so it does not push back on stretched valuations or step in when valuations crash.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: So, index funds can be a sensible choice for the individual and the aggregate consequence of millions of those sensible choices can have changed the structural behavior in markets
claims.claim: Index funds are rational for individuals but the aggregate effect of price-insensitive capital changes market structure; the argument is structural, not about whether to own index funds.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: the price sensitive participants have been displaced by price insensitive ones
claims.claim: The share of price-sensitive agents has shrunk because passive displaced them, even though active capital remains large in absolute terms.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: There's what I call reinforcing feedback and this is where the feedback amplifies movements. And there's balancing feedback.
claims.claim: Two feedbacks run through markets: reinforcing (amplifies moves: momentum, stop losses, vol targeting, index inclusion) and balancing (absorbs moves: value, counter-trend, market makers); their interplay decides trend, range or break.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: what passive has done by design, not by accident, is it's to reduce the share of the market doing the balancing work.
claims.claim: Passive reduces the share of capital doing balancing work while forced index-inclusion and rebalancing flows have grown.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: Reinforcing feedback comes from divergent traders and from passive long only investors.
claims.claim: Divergent traders (trend, momentum) and passive long-only are on the reinforcing side; convergent traders (value, mean reversion, counter-trend) provide balancing, and that group has been diluted.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: trends now run further before they meet resistance because the resistance is structurally smaller
claims.claim: With less balancing capital, markets are more prone to extended directional moves, overshoot and cascades, because balancing is weaker rather than reinforcing being stronger.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: So, when the price sensitive capital does move, its impact on price is larger than it would have been 20 years ago.
claims.claim: Price-sensitive capital operates in a thinner float because most shares are held by price-insensitive holders, so its price impact is larger and markets are structurally inelastic.
claims.direction: bigger moves per unit of flow
claims.testable: yes - price impact per dollar of flow over time

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: The structural change is the transfer of a growing share of market ownership from price sensitive agents to price insensitive ones.
claims.claim: The key structural change of two decades is the shift from price-sensitive to price-insensitive ownership, more than HFT, algos or mega-cap dominance, which are downstream effects.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I wonder to some extent when if they have kind of filled up a little bit of the role that other sort of convergent strategies may have filled
claims.claim: Host's question: structured-product issuance that suppresses volatility may be acting as a convergent force that partly offsets passive's effect.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: because of this leverage that's introduced into this calm environment because investors have got to make the return somehow
claims.claim: In calm low-volatility regimes strategies concentrate and lever up (including via structured products), losing diversity and building fragility.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: So when you get a small deviation out of that that structural calm, a small deviation, you suddenly get this non-linear amplification
claims.claim: After concentrated leveraged positioning in a calm regime, a small deviation triggers non-linear amplification and a large breakout.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: and they were essentially probably often trading against the trend followers and keeping markets from breaking up
claims.claim: Pod shops and multi-strategy funds probably traded against trend followers and held markets in range; when markets break out they are caught on the wrong side, amplifying the move (host observation, no evidence).

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: theoretically an extinction level event of passive
claims.claim: Concentration into passive could end in an extinction-level unwind, as complex adaptive systems alternate growth phases with extinction.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: what works against passive it's to some degree is demography
claims.claim: Demography (retirees drawing down passive holdings) is the force that may eventually reverse passive growth, probably affecting the next generation.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the winner um is not trend, unfortunately. But, with 59% respondents, it's discretionary global macro
claims.claim: SocGen spring 2026 investor survey: CTA trend rose two places from autumn 2025 but investor interest is led by discretionary global macro (59%), commodities (43%), equity market neutral (42%); CTA trend 29%.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the pot shops are not as popular as they were only about a year ago
claims.claim: Interest in multi-strategy systematic managers fell to the lowest rank of the last five surveys.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: It's down to 39% which it hasn't touched for quite a while
claims.claim: The TTU Trend Barometer fell to 39% at end of May 2026, signalling trend weakness after a late-month correction (oil down over 5% in a week).

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: SocGen CTA index up 72 basis points in May up 11% for the year
claims.claim: Data for May 2026: SG CTA +0.72% (+11% YTD), SG Trend +1.07% (+11.31% YTD), short-term traders +0.25% (+5.5% YTD), MSCI World +3.8% May (about +10% YTD), US agg bond flat (+0.28% YTD), S&P 500 +4.43% May (+10.38% YTD).
claims.indicator: SG CTA, SG Trend, MSCI World, S&P 500

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: I'm finding it's a very good leading indicator.
claims.claim: Brennan finds the short-timeframe Trend Barometer a good directional leading indicator for his own lagging trend fund.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it actually has a an extraordinary way of giving you an indication of what was the month like
claims.claim: The Barometer (unchanged since 2007) is not a good trading tool but at month end it describes whether the month was a good or bad trend environment because of its look-back.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: every position, for example, in my program is sized by average true range, ATR, which is a direct measure of the instrument's own variance.
claims.claim: Trend following already controls instrument variance: ATR sizing shrinks a position automatically when variance rises, plus portfolio vol targeting and position-level drawdown management.
claims.direction: reduce size when instrument variance rises

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: Correlation is the diagnostic. It tells me what the system is doing. Variance is the control.
claims.claim: Correlation shows how shocks travel across instruments (diagnostic); variance within instruments is the control for sizing, cutting and backing off; a trend follower needs both.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: The structure lives in the interactions, not in the components.
claims.claim: Like a starling flock following local rules, market structure (trends, crashes, volatility clustering, concentration) is emergent from interactions, with no participant intending the outcome.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: So, the equilibrium model treats markets as though they are clocks, not flocks.
claims.claim: Classical equilibrium finance treats markets as physical systems and deviations from fair value as noise; real participants observe and imitate each other, so this is a category error.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: So, the equilibrium model has survived because it's convenient, not because it's right.
claims.claim: The equilibrium model persists because it gives spreadsheets and portfolio methods, whereas the feedback view requires a research programme.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: But the size and duration of the move are often determined less by the news than by the internal feedback that the news activates in the system
claims.claim: News acts as a trigger but move size and duration depend on internal feedback ('the match starts the fire; the wood's dryness determines its extent').

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: The vast majority of price movement can't be attributed to identifiable news.
claims.claim: Microstructure research (Bouchaud, Gabaix, Cohen) finds most price movement cannot be linked to news; large moves occur without proportional catalysts.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: Most price movement is not driven by anything coming from outside the system. It's driven by the system processing itself.
claims.claim: The endogenous engine: price changes behavior and behavior changes price (breakout draws in momentum, which alters volatility, triggering vol targeting and rebalancing), and the cascade matters more than the spark.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: Their reactions reshape the markets which reshape the next observation which reshape the next reaction.
claims.claim: Reflexivity (Soros): price-sensitive participants' reactions reshape the market they observe, a recursive loop that passive participants are not part of.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: Because the endogenous engine keeps running long after the trigger has faded.
claims.claim: Trends persist beyond any single catalyst because the feedback loop outlasts the trigger.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: Because there is no force in the system pulling them toward it.
claims.claim: Markets overshoot fundamental value because fundamentals live in a separate system and nothing in the market forces convergence; the largest moves occur when the architecture is sensitised.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: A small buy order nudges price upward. That nudge activates trading systems buy what is rising.
claims.claim: Reinforcing feedback: a small order triggers trend systems, model recalibration, institutional rebalancing and late performance chasers, forming directional patterns (the fuel of trends).

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: Market makers quote both sides of the book. Value investors step in when prices fall below perceived worth.
claims.claim: Balancing feedback (market makers, value investors, risk managers) absorbs moves and creates temporary zones of calm; without it reinforcing loops would grow until collapse.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: When reinforcing loops dominate, the system becomes directional in trends form. When balancing loops dominate, the system becomes range bound.
claims.claim: Reinforcing-dominated regimes trend and balancing-dominated regimes range; when influence shifts rapidly, phase transitions occur and volatility surges.
claims.direction: trend following in reinforcing regimes, fails in ranges
claims.conditions: regime depends on balance of feedbacks

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: the options dealer who must delta hedge in the direction of the move
claims.claim: Reinforcing agents include momentum chasers, stop losses, vol-targeting funds, passive cap-weighted buying, dealers delta-hedging with the move and forced index-inclusion buying.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: But, what passive does is dilute their share of the ecology.
claims.claim: Passive does not eliminate balancing agents but dilutes their proportional weight, so reinforcing loops run further before meeting resistance, and the S&P rises while fundamentals weaken.
claims.indicator: balancing agent share, S&P 500 vs fundamentals

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: the effective pool available to absorb active buying or selling, the price sensitive agents, is structurally thin
claims.claim: Market inelasticity: when most shares are held by price-insensitive holders, the price-sensitive pool absorbing active flow is thin.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: $1 of net buying can increase aggregate market capitalization by approximately $5.
claims.claim: Inelastic-markets studies suggest the flow multiplier is about 5 (range 3-7): $1 of net buying lifts market cap by about $5 and $1 of selling destroys about $5.
claims.testable: yes - published estimates, multiplier varies by study

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: runs from roughly three to one at the conservative end to closer to seven to one in the more aggressive estimates
claims.claim: The multiplier range is 3x to 7x depending on method; the structural fact is that it is much larger than classical finance assumed.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: The inner elasticity ensures that the trends that produces are larger than the flows that created them.
claims.claim: Inelasticity makes feedback-driven trends larger than the flows that started them, so the same dollar of buying moves price more than it did 20 years ago.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: the statistical fingerprint fingerprint of of feedback-driven markets across 40 years and 68 markets
claims.claim: Brennan's 'factors of finance' research examines the statistical fingerprint of feedback across 68 futures markets over 40 years.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: They're like us, divergent traders, agents whose behavior, conditioned on recent price action
claims.claim: Agent-based model: chartist (divergent, reinforcing) agents versus fundamentalist (convergent, balancing) agents with one knob for the chartist share from 0% to 100%.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: The Hurst exponent sat at um about 0.54. That was statistically indistinguishable from a random walk.
claims.claim: With zero chartists the simulated market behaves like classical finance (Hurst about 0.54, excess kurtosis -0.2, no five-sigma events, no volatility clustering).

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: we only needed to put 25% chartists who are price sensitive working in the reinforcing direction to create this phase transition in the market structure
claims.claim: Around 20-25% reinforcing agents produce a phase transition (kurtosis erupts, Hurst above 0.85, fat tails and volatility clustering appear at once).

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: the Hurst exponent's just a measure of memory in a time series
claims.claim: Hurst near 0.5 means no memory, above 0.5 means persistence; kurtosis measures fat tails; these two statistics are used as the feedback fingerprint.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: it became statistically indistinguishable from the 68 real futures markets spanning eight asset classes, six continents, 41 years of trading history
claims.claim: Above the critical threshold the simulated market matches the fingerprint of 68 real futures markets across eight asset classes, 41 years, with no news or fundamentals.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: So, the controlled experiment shows that feedback is sufficient to generate the statistical signatures we observe.
claims.claim: Feedback alone is sufficient to generate the statistical signatures (trending, fat tails, volatility clustering), and is the central mechanism rather than a minor one.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: Stop loss orders are feedback. Margin calls are feedback. Volatility targeting is feedback.
claims.claim: Almost every active participant responds to price, so the reinforcing share is far above the 20-25% threshold, even when passive is about 60% of equities.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: It fluctuated between 0.62 and 0.82 responding to both crises and regime changes.
claims.claim: In rolling 5-year windows the Hurst exponent across 40 years never fell to 0.5 (range 0.62-0.82) and survived Black Monday, electronic trading, the GFC, HFT and COVID.
claims.testable: yes - rolling Hurst on futures data

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: then what trend following has been doing for those 40 years is not exploiting a temporary inefficiency.
claims.claim: Trend following harvests a structural feature of markets (the feedback engine) that has never weakened since 1985, rather than a temporary inefficiency.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: the architecture is not weakening, it's hardening.
claims.claim: Because passive dilutes balancing agents while leaving reinforcing ones intact, the flow is thinner and the multiplier higher, so the same fingerprint appears with more violence per unit of flow.
claims.testable: partly - needs time series of the fingerprint

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: what we found was that the fraction averaged.6 persistently across the entire 40-year sample
claims.claim: The 68 futures markets share feedback sign more than independence would imply (0.60 average vs 0.55 expected, up to 0.82), i.e. one permanently coupled feedback engine.
claims.indicator: cross-market share of majority feedback sign

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: Many of the same investors apply the same models across many of the same markets.
claims.claim: Cross-market coupling arises because systematic capital applies correlated models across asset classes, so a buy signal in one market often appears in another.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: So, during crisis episodes, the system collectively tilts posture towards positive feedback and trends emerge. But during quantitative easing suppressed regimes, the system collectively tilts towards negative feedback and oscillation emerges.
claims.claim: Crises tilt the coupled system toward positive feedback and trends, while QE-suppressed regimes tilt it toward negative feedback and oscillation.
claims.direction: trends in crises, mean reversion in QE regimes
claims.testable: yes - feedback state by macro regime
